Rashi on Shabbat 33a:10:1.hebrew: הממרק עצמו - מפנה לבו לכך, ממרק עצמו משאר עסקים להתעסק בעבירות:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:10:1.english: One who clears himself - He directs his mind to this; he frees himself from other pursuits to engage in sins.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:10:2.english: Purge evil - One who purges [himself] for evil.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:11:1.hebrew: תפוח - שייני"ס, נפוח עורו על בשרו, ומים בינתיים, ונראה כזכוכית ורך מתוכו:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:11:1.english: Swollen - [*seinis*] — his skin is swollen over his flesh, and [there is] water in between, and it appears like glass, and is soft from within.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:11:2.english: Thin - His flesh is thin and emaciated.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:11:3.hebrew: של עבירה עבה - הבאה בשביל עבירה. עבה — בשרו מתקשה ועב, ונפוח בעובי:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:11:3.english: [The one] for sin is thick - [The dropsy] that comes on account of sin. "Thick" — his flesh becomes hardened and thick, and swollen in thickness.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:12:1.hebrew: מי מפיס - מי מטיל גורל להבחין ולהודיע שאינו של עבירה? עכשיו יאמרו עלי שעברתי על דת, ואין הכל יודעין בג' סימנים שאמרנו, ופעמים שמשתנין:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:12:1.english: Who will draw lots - Who will cast lots to distinguish and make known that this illness is not on account of sin? Now people will say about me that I transgressed the law, and not everyone knows the three signs that we mentioned, and sometimes they vary.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:12:2.hebrew: ידענא ביה - שמחמת רעב בא לו, ואין צריך לחשדו:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:12:2.english: I know about him - That it came upon him on account of hunger, and there is no need to suspect him [of sin].

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:12:3.hebrew: והא רבא דאמר - כלומר, למה חש בו? והא לא הרעיב את עצמו, מדקאמר: ״ידענא ביה בנחמני״, מכלל דהמרעיב עצמו רע בעיניו. ואי משום שהיה משהה נקביו — ואמרינן בבכורות (דף סד:): ״צואה רבה, הדרוקן רבה״ — שעל שהיית נקבים הוא בא:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:12:3.english: And behold, Rava said - That is to say, why did he fall ill with it? Behold, he did not starve himself, since he said: “I know about Naḥmani,” from which it follows that starving oneself is bad in his eyes. And if it was because he delayed relieving his orifices — and we say in Bekhorot (page 64b): “Much excrement, much dropsy,” for it comes on account of delaying to relieve one's orifices.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:12:4.hebrew: הא איהו אמר נפישי קטילי קדר - רבים הרוגי נקבים ממותי הדרוקן של רעב. קדר — לשון קדרה, על שם ששופך כקדרה:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:12:4.english: Did he not say: "More are those killed by the pot" - Those killed by [holding back their] bodily excretions are more numerous than those who die of the dropsy of hunger. Kedar is an expression for a pot [kedera], so called because one pours [it] out like a pot.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:12:5.hebrew: דאנסי ליה רבנן בעידניה - התלמידים הקבועים להם עת לפניו, אונסין אותו להשהות נקביו:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:12:5.english: Because the Rabbis compel him during his time - The students, who have a set time before him, compel him to delay [relieving] his orifices.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:13:1.hebrew: סימן לגסות הרוח עניות - בפרק האיש מקדש (קדושין דף מט:) מפרש: מאי עניות? עניות דתורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:13:1.english: A sign of arrogance is poverty - In the chapter [entitled] HaIsh Mekadesh (Kiddushin 49b), [the Gemara] explains: What is [meant by] poverty? Poverty of Torah [knowledge]:

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:13:2.hebrew: אסכרה - חולי המתחיל במעיים וגומר בגרון, הנקרא בונמלא"ן:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:13:2.english: Askara - An illness that begins in the intestines and ends in the throat, which is called bon malan [in Old French, i.e., diphtheria].

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:1:1.hebrew: דאכלן ולא עבדן - ונמצא שגוזלות את בעליהן. ועוד: מתוך שמלומדות במאכל ובמשתה, גורמות לבעלים לגזול:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:1:1.english: Who eat and do not work - And it turns out that they rob their husbands. And furthermore, since they are accustomed to food and drink, they cause [their] husbands to rob.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:1:2.hebrew: וכתיב - בההיא פרשה בנבואת עמוס: ״הכיתי אתכם בשדפון״, וסיפיה דקרא: ״כרמיכם וזיתיכם יאכל הגזם״. וכתיב ביואל: ״יתר הגזם״, דמשמע שהגזם אינו אלא תחלת מכה, ואחריה באים ארבה וחסיל — אלמא גובאי עולה בעון גזל. וכיון דמיני גובאי עולין, רעב הוה; וכיון דהרעב הוה, כתיב בישעיה: ״ויגזור על ימין ורעב״ וגו', וסיפיה דקרא: ״איש בשר זרועו יאכלו״:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:1:2.english: And it is written - In that [same] passage in the prophecy of Amos: “I have smitten you with blight,” and the end of the verse [is]: “your vineyards and your olive trees has the palmerworm devoured.” And it is written in Joel: “That which the palmerworm has left,” which implies that the palmerworm is only the beginning of the plague, and after it come the locust and the caterpillar — thus [it is shown that] locusts come up due to the sin of robbery. And since species of locust come up, famine ensues; and since famine ensues, it is written in Isaiah: “And one snatches on the right hand, and is hungry,” etc., and the end of the verse [is]: “they eat every man the flesh of his own arm.”

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:2:1.hebrew: עינוי הדין - שמאחרין הדיינין לדונו, ולא לשם שמים, אלא לאחר שהוברר להן הדין, משהין אותו:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:2:1.english: Delay of justice - That the judges delay adjudicating it, and not for the sake of Heaven, but rather, after the ruling has become clear to them, they delay it.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:2:2.english: Distortion of justice - That they intentionally distort it.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:2:3.hebrew: קלקול הדין - שלא היו מתונין בו לעיין כל צרכן, ונתקלקל מאליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:2:3.english: Miscarriage of justice - That [the judges] were not deliberate in it to examine [it] as much as needed, and it became corrupted on its own.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:2:4.hebrew: חרב וביזה רבה כו' - דכתיב: ״נקם ברית״, ואין ״ברית״ אלא תורה, דכתיב: ״אם לא בריתי יומם ולילה״ — וכתיב: ״והגית בו יומם ולילה״. וכתיב: ״חרב״ — ועל ידי חרב, דהיינו משלחת גירוי מלחמה, הביזה באה. וכתיב: ״ושלחתי דבר״ — הרי דבר. וכתיב: ״בשברי לכם מטה לחם״ — הרי בצורת. וכתיב בסוף כל הקללות: ״יען וביען במשפטי מאסו״ — הרי עינוי, ועיוות, וקלקול בכלל:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:2:4.english: The sword and looting abound, etc. - As it is written: “[that shall execute the] vengeance of the covenant,” and “covenant” means nothing other than Torah, as it is written: “If My covenant be not with day and night,” [and it is written:] “and you shall meditate upon it day and night.” And it is written: “a sword” — and through the sword, that is, the dispatching of the instigation of war, looting comes. And it is written: “and I will send pestilence [among you]” — behold, pestilence [is mentioned]. And it is written: “When I break your staff of bread” — behold, famine [is mentioned]. And it is written at the end of all the curses: “Even because they rejected My ordinances” — behold, delay [of justice], distortion [of justice], and miscarriage [of justice] are included.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:3:1.hebrew: שבועות שוא - כל המשנה את הידוע, כגון על האיש שהוא אשה. שבועת שקר — שאין בדאותו ניכרת, ומאמין שקר לבריות:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:3:1.english: Oaths in vain - Any [oath] that contradicts that which is known, such as [swearing] about a man that he is a woman. A false oath [is one] whose fabrication is not evident, and he causes people to believe a falsehood.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:3:2.english: And the roads become desolate - For lack of [any] passerby.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:3:3.hebrew: אלא באלה - ויש במשמע בין שוא בין שקר. וכתיב בשבועת שקר "וחללת", ובשבת ובחילול השם כתיב "חילול", וגמרינן משבועה:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:3:3.english: Rather, [due to] an oath - And [the term] implies both [an oath in] vain and a false [oath]. And it is written regarding a false oath: “And you shall profane,” and regarding Shabbat and desecration of the Name it is written “desecration,” and we derive [them] from [the] oath.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:3:4.hebrew: חילול השם - אדם גדול שבני אדם למדים הימנו, ואינו נזהר במעשיו — נמצאו הקטנים מזלזלין בתורה על ידו, ואומרים: זהו מבין שאין ממש בתורה ובמצות. ונמצא השם מתחלל — נעשה דבריו חולין:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:3:4.english: Desecration of the Name - A great person from whom people learn, who is not careful in his actions — the lesser [people] consequently treat the Torah disrespectfully on his account, and say: "This [scholar] understands that there is no substance to the Torah and the commandments"; and [God's] Name is consequently desecrated — His words have been rendered profane.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:4:1.hebrew: אין אני שוכן - חורבן הבית במשמע, שאין משכני בתוכם:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:4:1.english: I do not dwell - The destruction of the Temple is implied, that My dwelling is not among them.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:5:1.english: For all these abominations - It is written in the section of [forbidden] sexual relations.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:6:1.hebrew: ונתתי את פגריכם על פגרי גלוליכם - דהיינו ע"ז, וכתיב בתריה: ״ואתכם אזרה בגוים״, וכתיב: ״ושממו עליה אויביכם היושבים בה״ — הרי שהם גולין, ואויביהם יושבין במקומן:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:6:1.english: And I will cast your carcasses upon the carcasses of your idols - That is, idol worship. And it is written after it: “And you will I scatter among the nations,” and it is written: “And your enemies who dwell therein shall be astonished at it” — behold, they are exiled and their enemies dwell in their place.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:7:2.hebrew: ואתם בארץ אויביכם - ולעיל מיניה כתיב: ״ושממו עליה אויביכם״:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:7:2.english: And you are in your enemies’ land - And earlier in the passage it is written: “And your enemies shall be desolate over it.”

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:8:1.hebrew: לא ישמח - הרי צרות וגזירות. "ואת יתומיו ואת אלמנותיו לא ירחם" — הרי צועקין ואינם נענין. בעון מה? "כי כלו חנף ומרע וכל פה דובר נבלה". "ועוד ידו נטויה" — לשון "ועד": כל שנותיו של אדם, שהן ע' שנה, יד הדין נטויה עליו לבטל זכיותיו בעון זה:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:8:1.english: Shall have no joy - Behold, [this refers to] troubles and decrees. “Neither shall He have compassion on their fatherless and widows” — behold, they cry out and are not answered. On account of what sin? “For everyone is ungodly and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks wantonness.” “And His hand is stretched out still” — [this is] in the sense of “and until” [וְעַד]: [throughout] all the years of a person, which are seventy years, the hand of [strict] justice is stretched out over him to nullify his merits on account of this sin.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:9:1.hebrew: הכל יודעין כו' - ולא הוצרך לאדם לפרש למה נכנסה, והמנבל פיו בכך — אפילו כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:9:1.english: Everybody knows, etc. - And there is no need for a person to explain why she entered, and one who speaks vulgarly about this — even [etc.].

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:9:2.hebrew: שוחה עמוקה - מוכנת לפי זרות, למי שפיו זרה:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:9:2.english: A deep pit - [It is] prepared for “a mouth of strange things” — for one whose mouth is perverse.

Rashi on Shabbat 33a:9:3.hebrew: זעום ה' יפול שם - זעם של הקב"ה הוא שורה שם, אצל פי זרות. היושב אצלו ושומע קרוי זעומו של הקב"ה:
Rashi on Shabbat 33a:9:3.english: He that is abhorred of the Lord shall fall therein - The wrath of the Holy One, Blessed be He, rests there, beside the “mouth that speaks perversity”; one who sits beside him and listens is called the abhorred of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
